title.zh: 卷一百八十 列傳第六十七: 耶律希亮 趙世延 孔思晦
title.en: Volume 180 Biographies 67: Yelu Xiliang, Zhao Shiyan, Kong Sihui
title.raw: 卷一百八十 列傳第六十七: 耶律希亮 趙世延 孔思晦 Volume 180 Biographies 67: Yelu Xiliang, Zhao Shiyan, Kong Sihui

sentences.zh: 耶律希亮

translations.literal: Yelu Xiliang
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiliang

sentences.zh: 耶律希亮，字明甫，楚材之孫，鑄之子也。

translations.literal: Yelu Xiliang, style name Mingfu, was the grandson of Yelü Chucai and the son of Yelü Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Xiliang, whose style name was Mingfu, was a grandson of Yelü Chucai and the son of Yelü Zhu.

sentences.zh: 初，六皇后命以赤帖吉氏歸鑄，生希亮於和林南之涼樓，曰禿忽思，六皇后遂以其地名之。

translations.literal: At first the Sixth Empress Dowager ordered that a woman of the Chiteji clan be given to Zhu in marriage; Xiliang was born at Lianglou south of Karakorum, called Tuhusi, and the Sixth Empress Dowager thereupon named him after that place.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning the Sixth Empress Dowager had a woman of the Chiteji clan given to Zhu in marriage. Xiliang was born at Lianglou south of Karakorum and was called Tuhusi; the Sixth Empress Dowager then gave him this place-name.

sentences.zh: 憲宗嘗遣鑄核錢糧於燕，鑄曰：「臣先世皆讀儒書，儒生俱在中土，願攜諸子，至燕受業。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong once sent Zhu to audit grain and funds in Yan. Zhu said, "My forebears for generations all read Confucian books; Confucian scholars are all in the Central Plains. I wish to bring my sons to Yan to receive instruction."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong once dispatched Zhu to verify grain and tax accounts in Yan. Zhu said, "For generations my ancestors studied the Confucian classics, and all the scholars are in the Central Plains. I ask leave to bring my sons to Yan to pursue their studies."

sentences.zh: 」憲宗從之，乃命希亮師事北平趙衍。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong agreed and thereupon ordered Xiliang to take Zhao Yan of Beiping as his teacher.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consented and appointed Xiliang to study under Zhao Yan of Beiping.

sentences.zh: 時方九歲，未浹旬，已能賦詩。

translations.literal: He was then just nine years old; before ten days had passed he could already compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He was only nine at the time, yet within ten days he could already write verse.

sentences.zh: 歲丙辰，憲宗召鑄還和林，希亮獨留燕。

translations.literal: In the year bingchen Emperor Xianzong summoned Zhu back to Karakorum; Xiliang alone remained in Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year the emperor recalled Zhu to Karakorum, and Xiliang stayed behind in Yan by himself.

sentences.zh: 歲戊午，憲宗在六盤山，希亮詣行在所。

translations.literal: In the year wuwu Emperor Xianzong was at Liupanshan; Xiliang went to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year, while the emperor was encamped at Liupanshan, Xiliang came to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 已而鑄扈從南伐，希亮亦在行。

translations.literal: Before long Zhu followed the southern campaign as an attendant, and Xiliang was also on the march.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhu accompanied the southern expedition, and Xiliang marched with them.

sentences.zh: 明年，憲宗崩於蜀，希亮將輜重北歸陝右。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Xianzong died in Shu; Xiliang escorted the baggage train north back to the Shaanxi region.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor died in Shu, and Xiliang led the supply train northward into Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 又明年，為中統元年，世祖即位，阿里不哥反，遣使召主將渾都海。

translations.literal: The year after that was the first year of Zhongtong; Emperor Shizu took the throne, Ariq Böke rebelled, and sent envoys to summon the commander-in-chief Hunduhai.
translations.idiomatic: Another year passed—the first year of the Zhongtong era. Kublai ascended the throne, Ariq Böke rose in revolt, and messengers were sent to summon the commander Hunduhai.

sentences.zh: 鑄說渾都海等入朝，皆不從，則棄其妻子，挺身來歸。

translations.literal: Zhu urged Hunduhai and the others to come to court; none obeyed, so he abandoned his wife and children and came alone to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu urged Hunduhai and his officers to present themselves at court, but they refused. He then left his family behind and came alone to Kublai's side.

sentences.zh: 既而渾都海知鑄去，怒，遣百騎追之不及。

translations.literal: When Hunduhai learned that Zhu had gone he was enraged and sent a hundred horsemen in pursuit, but they did not overtake him.
translations.idiomatic: When Hunduhai learned Zhu had fled, he flew into a rage and sent a hundred riders after him, but they failed to catch him.

sentences.zh: 乃使百人監視希亮母子，迫脅使從行，自靈武過應吉里城，至西涼甘州。

translations.literal: He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili city to Ganzhou in Xiliang.
translations.idiomatic: He then placed a hundred men to guard Xiliang and his mother, forcing them to march with the army from Lingwu through Yingjili to Ganzhou in the Western Liang region.

sentences.zh: 阿里不哥遣大將阿藍答兒自和林帥師至焉支山，希亮見之。

translations.literal: Ariq Böke sent the great general Alandar from Karakorum at the head of troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Böke dispatched the general Alandar from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, and Xiliang was brought before him.

sentences.zh: 阿藍答兒問：「而父安在？

translations.literal: Alandar asked, "Where is your father?"
translations.idiomatic: Alandar asked, "Where is your father?"

sentences.zh: 」希亮曰：「不知，與吾父同任事者宜知之。

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "I do not know; those who share office with my father ought to know."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang replied, "I do not know. Those who serve with my father should know."

sentences.zh: 」渾都海怒，詬曰：「我焉得知之，其父今亡命東見皇帝矣！

translations.literal: Hunduhai in anger reviled him, saying, "How should I know? His father has now fled east to see the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: Hunduhai burst out angrily, "How would I know? His father has already fled east to join the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 」希亮曰：「若然，則何謂不知！

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "If that is so, then what do you mean by not knowing!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "If that is so, what did you mean by not knowing?"

sentences.zh: 」阿藍答兒熟視渾都海曰：「此言深有意焉。

translations.literal: Alandar stared intently at Hunduhai and said, "These words carry deep meaning."
translations.idiomatic: Alandar fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "That remark was deeply pointed."

sentences.zh: 」詰希亮甚急。

translations.literal: He pressed Xiliang very urgently with questions.
translations.idiomatic: He then questioned Xiliang sharply.

sentences.zh: 希亮曰：「使吾知之，亦從而去，安得獨留！

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "If I had known, I would have gone away with him too—how could I alone have been left behind!"
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "Had I known, I would have gone with him. How could I have been left behind alone?"

sentences.zh: 」阿藍答兒以為實，免其監蒞。

translations.literal: Alandar took this as truth and released him from close guard.
translations.idiomatic: Alandar believed him and lifted the close surveillance.

sentences.zh: 既而阿藍答兒、渾都海為大兵所殺，其殘卒北走，眾推哈剌不花為帥。

translations.literal: Before long Alandar and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; the remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Qara Buqa commander.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Alandar and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Qara Buqa as their leader.

sentences.zh: 希亮潛匿甘州北黑水東沙陀中。

translations.literal: Xiliang hid secretly in the Shato region east of the Black River north of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang went into hiding in the Shato country east of the Black River, north of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 殿兵已過十餘里，有尋馬者適至，老婢漏言，眾奄至，驅至肅州。

translations.literal: The rearguard had already passed more than ten li when horse-seekers happened to arrive; an old maidservant let slip the secret, the crowd suddenly surrounded them, and they were driven to Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The rearguard had marched on more than ten li when scouts arrived. An old servant woman betrayed them, the party was seized, and they were taken to Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 哈剌不花與鑄有婚姻之好，又哈剌不花在蜀時，嘗疾病，鑄召醫視之,遺以酒食， 因釋希亮縛，謂曰：「我受恩於汝父，此圖報之秋也。

translations.literal: Qara Buqa and Zhu were joined by marriage ties; moreover when Qara Buqa was in Shu he had once fallen ill, and Zhu summoned a physician to treat him and sent wine and food. He therefore released Xiliang's bonds and said, "I received favor from your father—this is the season to repay it."
translations.idiomatic: Qara Buqa was related to Zhu by marriage, and when he had fallen ill in Shu, Zhu had sent a doctor and provisions. He therefore freed Xiliang and said, "Your father once showed me great kindness. Now is my chance to repay it."

sentences.zh: 」及抵沙州北川，希亮與兄弟徒步負任，不火食者數日。

translations.literal: When they reached the north pass of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers went on foot carrying their loads and went several days without cooked food.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached the northern route out of Shazhou, Xiliang and his brothers walked on foot carrying their burdens and went several days without a hot meal.

sentences.zh: 是冬，涉雪逾天山，至北庭都護府。

translations.literal: That winter they crossed snow over the Tianshan range and reached the Protectorate General of Beiting.
translations.idiomatic: That winter they crossed the snow-covered Tianshan and came to the Beiting protectorate headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二年，至昌八里城。

translations.literal: In the second year they reached the city of Changbali.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they reached Changbali.

sentences.zh: 夏，逾馬納思河，抵葉密里城，乃定宗潛邸湯沐之邑也。

translations.literal: In summer they crossed the Manas River and arrived at Yemili city—the fief where Emperor Dingzong had held his princely establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In summer they crossed the Manas River and reached Yemili, the appanage town of Ögedei's princely household.

sentences.zh: 時六皇后之妹主後位，與宗王火忽皆欲東覲。

translations.literal: At that time the younger sister of the Sixth Empress Dowager held the chief consort's position, and she and the prince Huohu both wished to go east to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: The Sixth Empress Dowager's younger sister then held the chief consort's rank, and she and Prince Huohu both wished to travel east to present themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 希亮母密知其事，攜希亮入見，已而事不果。

translations.literal: Xiliang's mother secretly learned of the matter, took Xiliang in to see her, but in the end the plan did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang's mother learned of the plan in secret and brought Xiliang in to see the empress, but the venture came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 冬，至於火孛之地。

translations.literal: In winter they reached the land of the Huo Bo.
translations.idiomatic: In winter they came to the territory of the Huo Bo.

sentences.zh: 三年，定宗幼子大名王閔其不能歸，遺以幣帛鞍馬，乃從大名王至忽只兒之地。

translations.literal: In the third year Dingzong's youngest son, Prince Daming, pitying that he could not return home, gave him silks, saddles, and horses; he then followed Prince Daming to Huzhier.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Prince Daming, the youngest son of Ögedei, took pity on his inability to return and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.

sentences.zh: 會宗王阿魯忽至，誅阿里不哥所用鎮守之人唆羅海，欲附世祖。

translations.literal: It happened that Prince Arigh Buqa arrived, executed Suoluo Hai whom Ariq Böke had placed in command, and wished to attach himself to Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Arigh Buqa then arrived, executed Suoluo Hai, whom Ariq Böke had installed as garrison commander, and sought to join Kublai.

sentences.zh: 復從大名王及阿魯忽二王還至葉密里城。

translations.literal: He again followed Princes Daming and Arigh Buqa back to Yemili city.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed the two princes, Daming and Arigh Buqa, back to Yemili.

sentences.zh: 王遺以耳環，其二珠大如榛，實價直千金，欲穿其耳使帶之。

translations.literal: The prince gave him ear-rings; the two pearls were as large as hazelnuts and were truly worth a thousand in gold; he wished to pierce his ears so he might wear them.
translations.idiomatic: The prince presented him with earrings set with pearls as large as hazelnuts, worth a thousand pieces of gold, and wished to pierce his ears so he could wear them.

sentences.zh: 希亮辭曰：「不敢因是以傷父母之遺體也。

translations.literal: Xiliang declined, saying, "I dare not for this reason injure the bodily form my parents bequeathed to me."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang declined, saying, "I dare not mutilate the body my parents gave me for this."

sentences.zh: 且無功受賞，於禮尤不可。

translations.literal: Moreover to receive reward without merit is especially impermissible by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, to accept a reward without having earned it would be utterly contrary to propriety.

sentences.zh: 」王又解金束帶遺之，且曰：「系此，於遺體宜無傷。

translations.literal: The prince again unfastened a gold girdle and gave it to him, saying, "Fasten this—it should not harm the bodily form bequeathed you."
translations.idiomatic: The prince then offered a gold belt instead, saying, "Wear this—it will not harm the body your parents gave you."

sentences.zh: 」五月，又為阿里不哥兵所驅，西行千五百里，至孛劣撒里之地。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they were again driven by Ariq Böke's troops, traveling west fifteen hundred li to Beliesali.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ariq Böke's troops drove them west again for fifteen hundred li to Beliesali.

sentences.zh: 六月，又西至換扎孫之地。

translations.literal: In the sixth month they went west again to Huanzhasun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month they marched farther west to Huanzhasun.

sentences.zh: 又從至不剌城。

translations.literal: They again followed on to Bula city.
translations.idiomatic: They continued on to Bula.

sentences.zh: 又西行六百里，至徹徹里澤剌之山，后妃輜重皆留於此，希亮母及兄弟亦在焉。

translations.literal: They went west another six hundred li to Checheli Zelai Mountain; the empresses' and consorts' baggage trains were all left here, and Xiliang's mother and brothers were also there.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled another six hundred li west to Checheli Zelai Mountain, where the imperial women's baggage was left behind, along with Xiliang's mother and brothers.

sentences.zh: 希亮單騎從行二百餘里，至出布兒城。

translations.literal: Xiliang alone on horseback followed the march more than two hundred li to Chubuer city.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang rode alone with the column for more than two hundred li to Chubuer.

sentences.zh: 又百里，至也裡虔城，而哈剌不花之兵奄至，希亮又從二王興師，還至不剌城，與哈剌不花戰，敗之，盡殲其眾。

translations.literal: Another hundred li to Yeliqian city, and Qara Buqa's troops suddenly arrived; Xiliang again followed the two princes in raising troops, returned to Bula city, fought Qara Buqa, defeated him, and annihilated his entire force.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred li brought them to Yeliqian, where Qara Buqa's army suddenly appeared. Xiliang again followed the two princes in raising troops, marched back to Bula, defeated Qara Buqa, and destroyed his force to the last man.

sentences.zh: 二王乃函其頭，遣使報捷。

translations.literal: The two princes then boxed his head and sent envoys to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: The two princes placed his head in a box and sent messengers to report the victory.

sentences.zh: 十月，至於亦思寬之地。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they reached Yisikuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month they reached Yisikuan.

sentences.zh: 四年，至可失哈里城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year they reached Kashgar.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year they came to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 四月，阿里不哥兵復至，希亮又從征，至渾八升城。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's troops came again; Xiliang again followed the campaign to Hunbasheng city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Ariq Böke's army returned, and Xiliang again joined the campaign as far as Hunbasheng.

sentences.zh: 時希亮母從後避暑於阿體八升山。

translations.literal: At that time Xiliang's mother followed in the rear to escape the heat at Atibasheng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile his mother had gone to the rear to escape the summer heat at Atibasheng Mountain.

sentences.zh: 先是，鑄嘗言於世祖：「臣之妻子皆在北邊。

translations.literal: Earlier Zhu had once said to Emperor Shizu, "Your servant's wife and children are all in the northern regions."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhu had told Kublai, "My wife and children are still in the north."

sentences.zh: 」至是，世祖遣不華出至二王所，因以璽書召希亮，馳驛赴闕。

translations.literal: At this time Emperor Shizu sent Buhua out to the two princes' camp and with an imperial seal-edict summoned Xiliang, who sped by post-horse to court.
translations.idiomatic: Now the emperor sent Buhua to the two princes with a sealed summons for Xiliang, who rode post-haste to court.

sentences.zh: 六月，由苦先城至哈剌火州，出伊州，涉大漠以還。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, from Kuxian city to Qarahoja, out through Yizhou, he crossed the great desert to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he traveled from Kuxian to Turfan, left by way of Yizhou, and crossed the great desert on his way home.

sentences.zh: 八月，入覲世祖於上都之大安閣，備陳邊事，及羈旅困苦之狀。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he had audience with Emperor Shizu at the Da'an Pavilion in Shangdu, fully reporting border affairs and the hardships of his long exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he presented himself to Kublai at the Da'an Pavilion in Shangdu and gave a full account of frontier affairs and the hardships of his years abroad.

sentences.zh: 世祖憐之，賜鈔千錠、金帶一、幣帛三十，命為速古兒赤、必阇赤。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu pitied him, bestowed a thousand ingots of paper money, one gold belt, and thirty pieces of silks, and appointed him sugurchi and bitikchi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him, gave him a thousand ingots of paper money, a gold belt, and thirty lengths of silk, and appointed him an imperial guard and court scribe.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，授奉訓大夫、符寶郎。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Gentleman for Admonition and Keeper of the Seals.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhiyuan era he was made Gentleman for Admonition and Keeper of the Imperial Seals.

sentences.zh: 十二年，既平宋，世祖命希亮問諸降將，日本可伐否。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, after the Song had been pacified, Emperor Shizu ordered Xiliang to ask the surrendered generals whether Japan could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, after the conquest of the Song, Kublai had Xiliang ask the surrendered generals whether Japan could be invaded.

sentences.zh: 夏貴、呂文煥、範文虎、陳奕等皆云可伐。

translations.literal: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhui, Chen Yi, and the others all said it could be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui, Lü Wenhuan, Fan Wenhui, Chen Yi, and the rest all said it could be done.

sentences.zh: 希亮奏曰：「宋與遼、金攻戰且三百年，干戈甫定，人得息肩，俟數年，興師未晚。

translations.literal: Xiliang memorialized, saying, "The Song fought Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years; arms have only just been laid down and the people have barely rested their shoulders—wait a few years and raising troops will not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang submitted, "The Song waged war against Liao and Jin for nearly three hundred years. Arms have only just been stilled and the people have barely caught their breath. To wait a few years before launching another campaign would not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」世祖然之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu approved this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十三年，太府監令史盧贄言於監官：「各路所貢布長三丈，唯平陽加一丈，諸怯薛歹以故爭取平陽布。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Taifu Commission clerk Lu Zan said to the supervising official, "The cloth presented from each circuit is three zhang in length, but Pingyang alone adds one zhang; for this reason the keshik compete for Pingyang cloth."
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Lu Zan, a clerk of the Imperial Household Commission, told his supervisor, "Each circuit sends cloth three zhang long, but Pingyang adds an extra zhang, so the imperial guards all scramble for Pingyang cloth."

sentences.zh: 苟截其長者，與他郡等，則無所爭，而以其所截者為髹漆宮殿器皿之用，甚便。

translations.literal: If the extra length were cut off to make it equal to other prefectures, there would be no contention, and the cut portions could be used for lacquered palace vessels—very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: If the surplus were trimmed so it matched the other regions, the rivalry would end, and the trimmed pieces could be used for lacquered palace furnishings—a great convenience.

sentences.zh: 」監官從之。

translations.literal: The supervising official followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor agreed.

sentences.zh: 適左右以其事聞，帝以詰監官，監官倉皇莫知所以對，歸罪於贄，帝命斬之。

translations.literal: Just then attendants reported the matter to the emperor, who questioned the supervising official; the official in panic did not know how to reply and shifted blame to Zan; the emperor ordered Zan beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants soon reported the matter to the emperor, who questioned the supervisor. Flustered and unable to answer, the man blamed Zan, and the emperor ordered Zan executed.

sentences.zh: 希亮遇諸途，贄以冤告。

translations.literal: Xiliang met him on the road; Zan pleaded his wrongful case.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang met him on the road, and Zan protested his innocence.

sentences.zh: 希亮命少緩，具以實入奏。

translations.literal: Xiliang ordered a brief delay and fully reported the facts in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang asked that the execution be delayed and submitted a full report of what had actually happened.

sentences.zh: 有旨令董文用讞之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dong Wenyong to judge the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Dong Wenyong to review the case.

sentences.zh: 竟釋贄，而召御史大夫塔察兒等讓之曰：「此事言官當言而不言，向微禿忽思，不誤誅此人耶！

translations.literal: In the end Zan was released, and the Censor-in-Chief Tachar and others were summoned and rebuked, saying, "On this matter the remonstrating officials ought to have spoken but did not—had it not been for Tuhusi, would not this man have been wrongly executed!"
translations.idiomatic: Zan was finally released, and the censor-in-chief Tachar and others were summoned and rebuked: "The censors should have spoken up about this. Had it not been for Tuhusi, would we not have executed an innocent man?"

sentences.zh: 」十四年，轉嘉議大夫、禮部尚書，尋遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Grand Master of Court Discussion and Minister of Rites, and soon moved to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion and Minister of Rites, and soon afterward became Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝駐蹕察納兒台之地，希亮至，奏對畢，董文用問大都近事。

translations.literal: The emperor was encamped at Chanai'ertai; when Xiliang arrived and finished his audience, Dong Wenyong asked about recent affairs in Dadu.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was encamped at Chanai'ertai, Xiliang arrived. After his audience Dong Wenyong asked him about recent events in the capital.

sentences.zh: 希亮曰：「囹圄多囚耳。

translations.literal: Xiliang said, "The prisons simply hold many prisoners."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang replied, "The prisons are simply overcrowded."

sentences.zh: 」世祖方欹枕而臥，忽寤，問其故。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu had been reclining on a pillow; he suddenly awoke and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had been dozing on his pillow; he started awake and asked why.

sentences.zh: 希亮奏曰：「近奉旨：漢人盜鈔六文者殺。

translations.literal: Xiliang memorialized, saying, "Recently there was an order: Han who steal six cash in paper money are to be killed."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang said, "A recent order decreed that any Han who steals six cash in paper money is to be executed."

sentences.zh: 以是囚多。

translations.literal: For this reason the prisoners are many.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the prisons are so full.

sentences.zh: 」帝驚問：「孰傳此語？

translations.literal: The emperor in alarm asked, "Who transmitted these words?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked in alarm, "Who spread that order?"

sentences.zh: 」省臣曰：「此旨實脫兒察所傳。

translations.literal: The provincial ministers said, "This order was in fact transmitted by To'ercha."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of the Secretariat said, "It was really To'ercha who circulated it."

sentences.zh: 」脫兒察曰：「陛下在南坡，以語蒙古兒童。

translations.literal: To'ercha said, "Your Majesty at Nanpo spoke thus to Mongol children."
translations.idiomatic: To'ercha said, "Your Majesty said this in jest to some Mongol boys at Nanpo."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「前言戲耳，曷嘗著為令式？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What I said before was only in jest—when was it ever set down as a statute?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That was only a joke. When did I ever make it a formal law?"

sentences.zh: 」乃罪脫兒察。

translations.literal: He then punished To'ercha.
translations.idiomatic: To'ercha was then punished.

sentences.zh: 希亮因奏曰：「令既出矣，必明其錯誤，以安民心。

translations.literal: Xiliang thereupon memorialized, saying, "Since the order has already gone forth, its error must be made clear to reassure the people's hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang then said, "Since the order has gone out, its mistake must be publicly corrected to reassure the people."

sentences.zh: 」帝善其言，即命希亮至大都，諭旨中書。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and at once ordered Xiliang to go to Dadu and proclaim the edict to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and immediately sent Xiliang to Dadu to announce the correction to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十七年，希亮以跋涉西土，足病痿攣，謝事而去，退居惣陽者二十餘年。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Xiliang, because of his long travels in the western regions, suffered paralysis of the legs and resigned his office; he retired to Zongyang for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, worn out by his years in the west and crippled by paralysis in his legs, he resigned and lived in retirement at Zongyang for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 至大二年，武宗訪求先朝舊臣，特除翰林學士承旨、資善大夫，尋改授翰林學士承旨、知制誥兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide Emperor Wuzong sought out old ministers of the previous reign and specially appointed him Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Palace Library; soon he was reassigned Academician Expositor-in-Chief, Drafter of Imperial Documents, and Compiler of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide era Emperor Wuzong sought out veterans of the previous reign and specially appointed him Academician Expositor-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Palace Library; he was soon given the additional posts of drafter of imperial documents and compiler of the national history.

sentences.zh: 希亮以職在史官，乃類次世祖嘉言善行以進，英宗取其書，置禁中。

translations.literal: Xiliang, since his office was among the historiographers, arranged and submitted Kublai's fine words and good deeds by category; Emperor Yingzong took his book and placed it within the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: As a historian he compiled Kublai's worthy sayings and deeds and presented them to the throne. Emperor Yingzong took the work and kept it in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 久之，閒居京師，四方之士多從之遊。

translations.literal: After a long while he lived at leisure in the capital, and scholars from all quarters often associated with him.
translations.idiomatic: He later lived in retirement in the capital, and scholars from every region came to study with him.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of the Taiding era at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 希亮性至孝，困厄遐方，家貲散亡已盡，僅藏祖考畫像，四時就穹廬陳列致奠，盡誠盡敬。

translations.literal: Xiliang's nature was supremely filial; though distressed in distant regions and his family wealth scattered and lost, he kept only portraits of his ancestors and forebears, and at each season set them out in his yurt to offer sacrifice with utmost sincerity and respect.
translations.idiomatic: Xiliang was profoundly filial. Though exiled far from home and stripped of his family's wealth, he kept only portraits of his ancestors and, at each season, set them out in his yurt to make offerings with the utmost devotion.

sentences.zh: 朔漠之人，咸相聚來觀，歎曰：「此中土之禮也。

translations.literal: The people of the northern deserts all gathered to watch and sighed, saying, "This is the ritual of the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: People of the northern steppe gathered to watch and marveled, "This is how they honor their ancestors in China."

sentences.zh: 」雖疾病，不廢書史，或中夜起坐，取燭以書。

translations.literal: Even when ill he did not abandon books and histories; sometimes he rose in the middle of the night, took a candle, and wrote.
translations.idiomatic: Even when ill he never stopped reading and writing; sometimes he would rise in the middle of the night, light a candle, and work on his books.

sentences.zh: 所著詩文及從軍紀行錄三十卷，目之曰《愫軒集》。

translations.literal: His collected poetry and prose and record of campaigns in thirty juan he titled the Su Studio Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry, prose, and military travelogue in thirty juan he called the Su Studio Collection.

sentences.zh: 贈推忠輔義守正功臣、資善大夫、集賢學士、上護軍，追封漆水郡公，諡忠嘉。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Supports Righteousness, and Upholds Integrity, Grand Master of the Palace Library, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Chief Guardian of the Army; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui and given the posthumous name Zhongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister of Loyalty and Righteousness, Grand Master of the Palace Library, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Chief Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui, and given the posthumous name Zhongjia.

sentences.zh: 趙世延

translations.literal: Zhao Shiyan
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan

sentences.zh: 趙世延，字子敬，其先雍古族人，居雲中北邊。

translations.literal: Zhao Shiyan, style name Zijing, his ancestors were Yonggu people dwelling on the northern border of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan, whose style name was Zijing, was descended from the Yonggu people and lived on the northern frontier of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖公，為金群牧使，太祖得其所牧馬，公死之。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Gong was Jin Director of Herds; when Taizu obtained the horses he pastured, Gong died for it.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Gong had been the Jin director of imperial herds. When Genghis Khan seized the horses under his care, Gong died defending them.

sentences.zh: 祖按竺邇，幼孤，鞠於外大父術要甲，訛為趙家，因氏為趙；

translations.literal: His grandfather Anzhuer, orphaned young, was reared by his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia; mistaken for the Zhao family, he therefore took Zhao as his surname;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Anzhuer was orphaned young and raised by his maternal grandfather Shuyao Jia. Taken for a member of the Zhao household, he adopted Zhao as his surname.

sentences.zh: 驍勇善騎射，從太祖征伐，有功，為蒙古漢軍徵行大元帥，鎮蜀，因家成都。

translations.literal: bold and skilled in riding and archery, he followed Taizu on campaigns, had merit, became Grand Marshal on Campaign of the Mongol Han Army, guarded Shu, and made his home in Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Brave and skilled in horsemanship and archery, he followed Genghis Khan on campaign, distinguished himself, and became grand marshal on campaign of the Mongol Han army. He was posted to guard Shu and settled his family in Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父黑梓，以門功襲父元帥職，兼文州吐?蚧Т锫郴ǔ唷?

translations.literal: His father Heizi, by hereditary military merit inherited his father's post as marshal and concurrently served as darughachi of the Wenz Prefecture Tibetan Ten-thousand Households Office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Heizi inherited the marshal's post through the family's military service and also held the post of darughachi at the Wenz Prefecture Tibetan Ten-thousand Households Office.

sentences.zh: 世延天資秀發，喜讀書，究心儒者體用之學。

translations.literal: Shiyan's natural endowment was brilliant; he delighted in reading books and devoted himself to the Confucian learning of substance and function.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyan was gifted by nature, loved books, and devoted himself to the Confucian pursuit of practical learning for the governance of the state.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，世祖召見，俾入樞密院御史臺肄習官政。

translations.literal: At his capping age Emperor Shizu summoned him for audience and had him enter the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Censorate to study official administration.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age Kublai received him in audience and had him train in government at the Bureau of Military Affairs and the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 至元二十一年，授承事郎、雲南諸路提刑按察司判官，時年二十有四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Langchengshilang and judge of the Yunnan Circuit Commission for Punishment and Investigation, aged twenty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 he was appointed court gentleman and judge of the Yunnan regional punishment and investigation commission, at the age of twenty-four.

sentences.zh: 烏蒙蠻酋叛，世延會省臣以軍討之，蠻兵大潰，即請降。

translations.literal: The Wumeng barbarian chieftain rebelled; Shiyan joined provincial officials with troops to attack him; the barbarian troops were greatly routed and immediately sought surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wumeng chieftain rebelled, Zhao Shiyan joined provincial officials in a military campaign; the rebel forces were routed and promptly surrendered.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，擢監察御史，與同列五人劾丞相桑哥不法。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was promoted to investigating censor and together with five colleagues in the same rank impeached Chancellor Sangge for unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: In 1289 he was promoted to investigating censor and, together with five colleagues, impeached Chancellor Sangge for misconduct.

sentences.zh: 中丞趙國輔，桑哥黨也，抑不以聞，更以告桑哥。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Guofu was of Sangge's faction; he suppressed the matter and did not report it upward, and instead informed Sangge.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhao Guofu, a member of Sangge's faction, suppressed the report and instead told Sangge directly.

sentences.zh: 於是五人者悉為其所擠，而世延獨倖免。

translations.literal: Thereupon all five were squeezed out by him, while Shiyan alone fortunately escaped.
translations.idiomatic: All five of his colleagues were driven from office, but Zhao Shiyan alone escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 奉旨按平陽郡監也先忽都贓巨萬，鞫左司郎中董仲威殺人獄，皆明允。

translations.literal: By imperial order he investigated Supervisor Yexianhudu of Pingyang Prefecture for bribes of tens of thousands, and tried the murder case of Left Department Director Dong Zhongwei—all were clear and equitable.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial commission he investigated the Pingyang supervisor Yexianhudu for embezzling vast sums and tried the murder case of Dong Zhongwei, director in the Left Department of the Secretariat—both judgments were fair and convincing.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，轉奉議大夫，出僉江南湖北道肅政廉訪司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Grand Master for Discussion and went out as concurrent commissioner of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit Commission for Upholding Justice and Investigating Visits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1292 he was appointed Grand Master for Discussion and sent out as deputy commissioner of the Jiangnan Huguang circuit censorate.

sentences.zh: 敦儒學，立義倉，撤淫祠，修澧陽縣壞堤，嚴常、澧掠賣良民之禁，部內晏然。

translations.literal: He promoted Confucian learning, established charity granaries, abolished improper shrines, repaired the broken dikes of Liyang County, strictly enforced the prohibitions on seizing and selling common people in Chang and Li, and the jurisdiction was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged Confucian learning, set up charity granaries, abolished improper shrines, repaired Liyang County's broken dikes, and strictly enforced bans on kidnapping and selling common people in Chang and Li—under his administration the region was at peace.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，除江南行御史臺都事，丁內艱，不赴。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was appointed director of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, but on his mother's death he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he was appointed director of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, but declined to take office when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，复除前官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he was again appointed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1297 he was reappointed to the same post.

sentences.zh: 三年，移中臺都事，俄改中書左司都事。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to director of the Central Branch Censorate, and soon after changed to director of the Left Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was transferred to the Central Branch Censorate and soon after to director of the Secretariat's Left Department.

sentences.zh: 臺臣奏，仍為都事中臺。

translations.literal: Censorate officials memorialized that he should still serve as director at the Central Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate petitioned that he remain as director at the Central Branch.

sentences.zh: 六年，由山東肅政廉訪副使改江南行臺治書侍御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was changed from deputy commissioner of the Shandong Commission for Upholding Justice to supervising secretary at the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1302 he moved from Shandong deputy censor to supervising secretary at the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 十年，除安西路總管。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed prefect of Anxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In 1306 he was appointed prefect of Anxi.

sentences.zh: 安西，故京兆省臺所治，號稱會府，前政壅滯者三千牘。

translations.literal: Anxi was formerly governed by the Jingzhao provincial administration and censorate, called a great metropolitan prefecture; the previous administration had congested three thousand dossiers.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi, once the seat of the Jingzhao province and its censorate, was known as a major administrative center; his predecessor had left three thousand cases backlogged.

sentences.zh: 世延既至，不三月，剖決殆盡。

translations.literal: When Shiyan arrived, within less than three months judgments were nearly all completed.
translations.idiomatic: Within three months of Zhao Shiyan's arrival, nearly all pending cases had been decided.

sentences.zh: 陝民飢，省臺議請於朝賑之，世延曰：「救荒如救火，願先發廩以賑，朝廷設不允，世延當傾家財若身以償。

translations.literal: The people of Shaanxi were starving; the provincial administration and censorate discussed requesting relief from court; Shiyan said: "Famine relief is like fighting fire; I wish first to open the granaries for relief; if the court should not approve, Shiyan will pledge his family wealth and person to make restitution."
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Shaanxi, the provincial authorities debated seeking court aid. Zhao Shiyan said, "Relieving famine is like fighting a fire—I beg that we open the granaries at once. If the court refuses, I will stake my fortune and my life to make good the cost."

sentences.zh: 」省臺從之，所活者眾。

translations.literal: The provincial administration and censorate followed this, and many were saved.
translations.idiomatic: The province and censorate agreed, and countless lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，除紹興路總管，改四川肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed prefect of Shaoxing Circuit and changed to commissioner of the Sichuan Commission for Upholding Justice and Investigating Visits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1308 he was appointed prefect of Shaoxing, then transferred to Sichuan censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 蒙古軍士，科差繁重，而軍士就戍往來者多害人，且軍官或抑良為奴，世延皆除其弊而正其罪。

translations.literal: Mongol soldiers had heavy taxes and corvée; soldiers going to and from garrison duty often harmed people, and military officers sometimes forced commoners into slavery; Shiyan removed all these abuses and punished the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol soldiers bore crushing levies, and troops traveling to and from garrison duty often preyed on civilians; some officers even forced commoners into slavery. Zhao Shiyan rooted out these abuses and punished the offenders.

sentences.zh: 又修都江堰，民尤便之。

translations.literal: He also repaired the Dujiangyan works, and the people found it especially convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He also repaired the Dujiangyan irrigation works, to the great benefit of the people.

sentences.zh: 四年，升中奉大夫、陝西行臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Second Rank and attendant censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In 1311 he was promoted to Grand Master of the Second Rank and attendant censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 先是，八百媳婦為邊患，右丞劉深往討之，兵敗而還，坐罪棄市。

translations.literal: Previously the Babai Xifu had been a border menace; Right Chancellor Liu Shen went to attack them, the army was defeated and returned, and he was executed by beheading at the market for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Babai Xifu had troubled the frontier; Right Chancellor Liu Shen led a campaign against them, was defeated, and was executed at the market for his failure.

sentences.zh: 及是，右丞阿忽台當繼行，世延言：「蠻夷事在羈縻，而重煩天討，致軍旅亡失，誅戮省臣，藉使盡得其地，何補於國？

translations.literal: At this time Right Chancellor Ahutai was about to succeed and go; Shiyan said: "Barbarian affairs lie in loose reins; yet repeatedly to trouble Heaven's punishment causes armies to be lost and provincial ministers to be executed—suppose we completely gained their land, what would it add to the state?"
translations.idiomatic: When Right Chancellor Ahutai was slated to lead the next campaign, Zhao Shiyan argued, "Barbarian affairs are best managed through loose reins. Repeated imperial expeditions cost us armies and ministers' lives—even if we conquered every inch of their territory, what would the empire gain?

sentences.zh: 今窮兵黷武，實傷聖治。

translations.literal: Now to exhaust the troops and abuse military force truly injures sagely governance.
translations.idiomatic: Endless warmaking now would only harm the sage rule of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 朝廷第當選重臣知治體者，付以邊寄，兵宜止勿用。

translations.literal: The court should only select weighty ministers who understand governing principles, entrust them with frontier responsibilities, and troops should cease and not be used.
translations.idiomatic: The court should appoint weighty ministers who understand governance to manage the frontier, and halt the use of force."

sentences.zh: 」事聞，樞密院臣以為用兵國家大事，不宜以一人之言為興輟。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Bureau of Military Affairs officials held that using troops was a great affair of state and should not be begun or halted on one man's words.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached court, officials of the Bureau of Military Affairs argued that war was too grave a matter to begin or end on one man's word.

sentences.zh: 世延聞之，章再上，事卒罷。

translations.literal: When Shiyan heard this, he memorialized again, and the affair ultimately ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan heard of this and submitted another memorial, and the campaign was finally abandoned.

sentences.zh: 皇慶二年，拜江浙行省參知政事，尋召還，拜侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangqing he was appointed vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, soon recalled, and appointed attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1313 he was made vice administrator of the Jiang-Zhe Secretariat, then recalled to serve as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年，省臣奏：「比奉詔漢人參政用儒者，趙世延其人也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou provincial officials memorialized: "Recently by edict Han Chinese vice administrators should use Confucians; Zhao Shiyan is such a man."
translations.idiomatic: In 1314 the provincial authorities memorialized, "By recent edict Han vice administrators should be scholars—Zhao Shiyan is such a man."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「世延誠可用，然雍古氏非漢人，其署宜居右。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Shiyan may indeed be used, yet the Yonggushi are not Han; his appointment rank should suitably be on the right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Zhao Shiyan is indeed capable, but as a man of Yonggu heritage he is not Han, so his formal rank must remain on the right."

sentences.zh: 」遂拜中書參知政事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed vice administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was accordingly appointed vice administrator of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 居中書二十月，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was in the Secretariat twenty months, then transferred to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty months at the Secretariat he was promoted to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 有旨省臣自平章以下，率送之官。

translations.literal: There was an order that Secretariat officials from pacification commissioner downward should all escort him to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict required every Secretariat official from the pacification commissioner down to escort him to his new post.

sentences.zh: 其禮前所無有，由是為權臣所忌，乃用皇太后旨，出世延為雲南行省右丞。

translations.literal: This ceremony had never existed before; thereby he was envied by powerful ministers, who then used the empress dowager's order to send Shiyan out as right vice administrator of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Such honor was unprecedented and earned him the enmity of powerful ministers, who secured an empress dowager's edict to transfer him to Yunnan as right vice administrator.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝特命仍還御史臺為中丞。

translations.literal: On farewell at the throne, the emperor specially ordered that he still return to the Censorate as vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of leave the emperor expressly commanded that he remain vice censor-in-chief at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 三年，世延劾奏權臣太師、右丞相帖木迭兒罪惡十有三，詔奪其官職。

translations.literal: In the third year Shiyan impeached and memorialized that the powerful minister Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Temuder had thirteen crimes; an edict stripped his offices.
translations.idiomatic: In 1316 Zhao Shiyan impeached Grand Preceptor and Right Chancellor Temuder on thirteen counts of misconduct, and an edict stripped him of office.

sentences.zh: 尋升翰林學士承旨，兼御史中丞，世延固辭，乃解中丞。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Expositor and concurrently vice censor-in-chief; Shiyan firmly declined, and then the censor post was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin expositor-in-chief, concurrently vice censor-in-chief, but Zhao Shiyan firmly declined the censorate and was relieved of that post.

sentences.zh: 五年，進光祿大夫、昭文館學士，守大都留守，乞補外，拜四川行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he advanced to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness, Zhao Wenguan academician, acting defender of Dadu, requested an outer appointment, and was appointed pacification commissioner of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1318 he was promoted to Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness and Zhao Wenguan academician, served as acting defender of Dadu, petitioned for a provincial post, and was appointed pacification commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 世延議即重慶路立屯田，物色江津、巴縣閒田七百八十三頃，摘軍千二百人墾之，歲得粟萬一千七百石。

translations.literal: Shiyan proposed immediately to establish military colonies at Chongqing Circuit, selected seven hundred eighty-three qing of idle land between Jiangjin and Baxian, detached twelve hundred soldiers to cultivate it, and yearly gained eleven thousand seven hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan proposed establishing garrison farms in Chongqing, identified 783 qing of unused land in Jiangjin and Baxian counties, assigned 1,200 troops to cultivate it, and harvested 11,700 shi of grain per year.

sentences.zh: 明年，仁宗崩，帖木迭兒复居相位，銳意報復，屬其黨何志道，誘世延從弟胥益兒哈呼誣告世延罪，逮世延置對，至夔路，遇赦。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Renzong died; Temuder again held the chancellorship, keenly intent on revenge, entrusted his faction member He Zhidao to induce Shiyan's younger cousin Xuyi'erhahu to falsely accuse Shiyan of crimes; Shiyan was arrested for interrogation, reached Kuizhou Circuit, and met an amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Renzong died and Temuder returned to power, bent on revenge. He had his follower He Zhidao induce Zhao Shiyan's cousin Xuyi'erhahu to lodge false charges; Shiyan was arrested and escorted toward trial, but was freed by an amnesty when he reached Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 世延以疾抵荊門，留就醫。

translations.literal: Shiyan because of illness reached Jingmen and stayed to seek treatment.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, Zhao Shiyan stopped at Jingmen to receive medical care.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒遣使督追至京師，俾其黨煅煉使成獄。

translations.literal: Temuder sent envoys to urge pursuit to the capital and had his faction forge and refine evidence to make the case complete.
translations.idiomatic: Temuder sent agents to hurry him to the capital and had his followers fabricate a conviction.

sentences.zh: 會有旨，事經赦原，勿復問。

translations.literal: There happened to be an order that matters passing through amnesty should be pardoned and not again investigated.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then came that cases covered by amnesty were not to be reopened.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒更以它事白帝，系之刑曹，逼令自裁，世延不為動，居囚再歲。

translations.literal: Temuder again reported other matters to the emperor, detained him in the penal office, forced him to take his own life; Shiyan was unmoved and dwelt in imprisonment two years.
translations.idiomatic: Temuder raised other charges and had him locked in the penal bureau, pressing him to suicide; Zhao Shiyan would not budge and spent two years in prison.

sentences.zh: 胥益兒哈呼自以所訴涉誣欺，亡去。

translations.literal: Xuyi'erhahu himself, because the accusation he made involved falsehood and deception, fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Xuyi'erhahu, realizing his testimony was fraudulent, fled.

sentences.zh: 中書左丞相拜住屢言世延亡辜，得旨出獄，就舍以養疾。

translations.literal: Left Chancellor of the Secretariat Baizhu repeatedly said Shiyan was without guilt; he received an order to leave prison and went to his lodging to nurse his illness.
translations.idiomatic: Left Chancellor Baizhu repeatedly pleaded Zhao Shiyan's innocence until an edict released him; he returned home to convalesce.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝獵北涼亭，顧謂侍臣曰：「趙世延先帝所尊禮，而帖木迭兒妄入其罪，數請誅之，此殆報私怨耳，朕豈能從之。

translations.literal: Previously, the emperor hunted at Beiliang Pavilion, turned and said to attending ministers: "Zhao Shiyan was honored by the former emperor, yet Temuder rashly entered crimes against him and several times requested his execution—this is probably repaying private grievances; how could I follow this?"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while hunting at Beiliang Pavilion, the emperor remarked to his attendants, "Zhao Shiyan was honored by my predecessor, yet Temuder fabricated charges and repeatedly sought his death—this is plainly private revenge, and I will never agree to it."

sentences.zh: 」侍臣皆叩頭稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The attending ministers all knocked their heads and cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants all prostrated themselves and shouted long life to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帖木迭兒在上京，聞世延出獄，索省牘視之，怒曰：「此左丞相罔上所為也。

translations.literal: Temuder was at Shangjing; hearing Shiyan left prison, he sought provincial documents to view them and angrily said: "This is the Left Chancellor deceiving the sovereign's doing."
translations.idiomatic: Temuder, then at Shangjing, learned of Shiyan's release, demanded the Secretariat records, and raged, "The Left Chancellor has deceived the throne into this."

sentences.zh: 」事聞，帝語之曰：「此朕意耳。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the emperor said to him: "This is My intention."
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the emperor, he told Temuder, "This was my own decision."

sentences.zh: 」未幾，帖木迭兒死，事乃釋。

translations.literal: Before long Temuder died and the affair was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Temuder died, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 世延出居於金陵。

translations.literal: Shiyan went out to dwell at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan retired to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，召還朝，除集賢大學士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was recalled to court and appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.
translations.idiomatic: In 1324 he was recalled and appointed Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為江南行臺御史中丞。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 四年，入朝，復為御史中丞，又遷中書右丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court, again became vice censor-in-chief, and was further transferred to right vice administrator of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he returned to court, was reappointed vice censor-in-chief, and then promoted to right vice administrator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，有旨：趙世延頃為權奸所誣，中書宜遍移天下，昭雪其非辜，仍加翰林學士承旨、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The next year there was an order: Zhao Shiyan had recently been falsely accused by powerful traitors; the Secretariat should broadly dispatch throughout the empire to clear his innocence, and additionally add Hanlin Academician Expositor and Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an edict declared that Zhao Shiyan had been slandered by power-hungry traitors, ordered the Secretariat to notify all regions to clear his name, and promoted him again to Hanlin expositor-in-chief with the rank of Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness.

sentences.zh: 經筵開，兼知經筵事，選揀勸講者，皆一時名流。

translations.literal: When the Classics Lectern opened, he was additionally put in charge of Classics Lectern affairs; those selected and chosen as exhorters and lecturers were all famous figures of the time.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial lecture program began, he was put in charge of it and chose lecturers from the leading scholars of the day.

sentences.zh: 又加同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 泰定帝崩，燕鐵木兒與宗王大臣議：武宗二子周王、懷王，於法當立；

translations.literal: When Emperor Taiding died, Yantuemuer and princes and great ministers deliberated: Emperor Wuzong's two sons the Prince of Zhou and the Prince of Huai, by law ought to be established;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiding died, Yantuemuer and the princes and senior ministers deliberated: by succession law Emperor Wuzong's sons, the Prince of Zhou and the Prince of Huai, should inherit the throne;

sentences.zh: 周王遠在朔漠，而懷王久居民間，備嘗艱險，民必歸之，天位不可久虛，不如先迎懷王，以從民望。

translations.literal: the Prince of Zhou was far away in the northern desert, while the Prince of Huai had long dwelt among the people, fully tasted hardship and peril, the people would surely turn to him, the Heavenly position could not long be empty—it was better first to welcome the Prince of Huai to follow the people's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: the Prince of Zhou was far away on the northern frontier, while the Prince of Huai had long lived among commoners and knew their hardships; the people would surely rally to him. The throne could not long lie vacant—better to welcome the Prince of Huai first and satisfy public expectation.

sentences.zh: 八月，即定策，迎之於江陵，懷王即位，是為文宗。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the plan was immediately settled; he was welcomed at Jiangling; the Prince of Huai took the throne—this is Emperor Wenzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the plan was set; the Prince of Huai was welcomed at Jiangling and enthroned as Emperor Wenzong.

sentences.zh: 當是時，世延贊畫之功為多。

translations.literal: At that time Shiyan's merit in planning and assistance was great.
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture Zhao Shiyan's role in planning the succession was decisive.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，世延仍以御史中丞兼翰林學士承旨，以疾乞歸田里，詔不允。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Shiyan still held vice censor-in-chief concurrently with Hanlin Academician Expositor; because of illness he requested to return to his fields, and an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's enthronement Zhao Shiyan remained vice censor-in-chief and Hanlin expositor-in-chief; he pleaded illness to retire, but the edict refused.

sentences.zh: 天曆二年正月，复除江南行臺御史中丞；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Tianli he was again appointed vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second Tianli year he was again appointed vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate;

sentences.zh: 行次濟州，三月，改集賢大學士；

translations.literal: traveling, he reached Jizhou; in the third month he was changed to Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents;
translations.idiomatic: en route he reached Jizhou; in the third month he was made Grand Academician of the Hall of Gathered Talents;

sentences.zh: 六月，又加奎章閣大學士；

translations.literal: in the sixth month he was additionally made Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion;
translations.idiomatic: in the sixth month he was additionally made Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion;

sentences.zh: 八月，拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: in the eighth month he was appointed pacification commissioner of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: in the eighth month he was appointed pacification commissioner of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 冬，世延至京，固辭不允，詔以世延年高多疾，許乘小車入內。

translations.literal: In winter Shiyan reached the capital; he firmly declined but was not permitted; an edict because Shiyan was advanced in years and frequently ill allowed him to ride a small carriage when entering within.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zhao Shiyan reached the capital and pleaded to decline office, but the court refused; noting his age and illness, an edict permitted him to ride a small carriage inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，詔世延與虞集等纂修《皇朝經世大典》，世延屢奏：「臣衰老，乞解中書政務，專意纂修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun an edict ordered Shiyan together with Yu Ji and others to compile the "Comprehensive Statutes of Imperial Governance"; Shiyan repeatedly memorialized: "Your servant is aged and feeble; I beg to be released from Secretariat governmental affairs to focus solely on compilation."
translations.idiomatic: In 1330 the court ordered Zhao Shiyan, Yu Ji, and others to compile the "Comprehensive Statutes of Imperial Governance." He repeatedly memorialized, "Your servant is old and weak; I beg to leave Secretariat duties and devote myself to compilation alone."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「老臣如卿者無幾，求退之言，後勿復陳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Old ministers like you are few; words seeking retirement—after this do not again present them."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Old ministers like you are few; do not raise retirement again."

sentences.zh: 」四月，仍加翰林學士承旨，封魯國公。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was still additionally Hanlin Academician Expositor and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was again made Hanlin expositor-in-chief and enfeoffed as Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 秋，以疾，移文中書致其事，明日即行，養疾於金陵之茅山。

translations.literal: In autumn, because of illness, he sent a document to the Secretariat to tender his resignation; the next day he set out and nursed his illness at Maoshan in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, citing illness, he sent notice to the Secretariat resigning his post; the next day he departed to recuperate on Maoshan in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 詔徵還朝，不能行，二年，改封涼國公。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him back to court but he could not travel; in the second year he was changed to Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled him to court, but he was too ill to travel; two years later his title was changed to Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，詔賜世延錢凡四萬緡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong an edict bestowed on Shiyan money totaling forty thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In 1334 the court granted Zhao Shiyan forty thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 至元改元，仍除奎章閣大學士、翰林學士承旨、中書平章政事、魯國公。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Zhiyuan he was still appointed Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, Hanlin Academician Expositor, pacification commissioner of the Secretariat, and Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: At the Yuan dynasty's restoration of the Zhiyuan reign title he was reappointed Grand Academician of the Kui Zhang Pavilion, Hanlin expositor-in-chief, pacification commissioner, and Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，至成都，十一月卒，享年七十有七。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, enjoying years seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The following May he reached Chengdu; in November he died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，贈世忠執法佐運翊亮功臣、太保、金紫光祿大夫、上柱國，追封魯國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng he was posthumously given the title of merit subject supporting loyalty through upholding law and assisting the fortune with bright aid, Grand Guardian, Grand Master of the Golden Bell and Purple Light, Upper Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Lu, posthumous name Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In 1342 he was posthumously ennobled as Supporting-Loyalty Merit Subject for Upholding Law and Assisting the Dynasty, Grand Guardian, Grand Master of the Golden Bell and Purple Radiance, Upper Pillar of the State, posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Lu with the temple name Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 世延歷事凡九朝，揚歷省臺五十餘年，負經濟之資，而將之以忠義，守之以清介，飾之以文學，凡軍國利病，生民休戚，知無不言，而於儒者名教尤拳拳焉。

translations.literal: Shiyan served through nine reigns in all, rose through provincial administration and censorate for more than fifty years, possessed talent for statecraft, yet led it with loyalty and righteousness, guarded it with pure integrity, adorned it with literary study—whatever benefited or harmed army and state, the welfare or woe of the people, he knew nothing he did not speak of, and toward the Confucian scholars' name and teaching he was especially earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shiyan served nine reigns and spent more than fifty years in provincial and censorial office. He possessed real talent for statecraft, tempered by loyalty and righteousness, guarded by integrity, and graced by learning. On every matter affecting army and state or the welfare of the people, he spoke without reserve; toward Confucian teaching he was especially devoted.

sentences.zh: 為文章波瀾浩瀚，一根於理。

translations.literal: His essays were vast in billows and surge, with one root in principle.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was sweeping in scope yet always grounded in principle.

sentences.zh: 嘗較定律令，匯次《風憲宏綱》，行於世。

translations.literal: He once compared and arranged laws and statutes, compiled the "Great Compendium of Censorial Regulations," which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He revised and collated statutes and compiled the "Great Compendium of Censorial Regulations," which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 五子，達者三人：野峻台，黃州路總管。

translations.literal: Five sons, three achieved prominence: Yejuntai, prefect of Huangzhou Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons, three of whom rose to office: Yejuntai, prefect of Huangzhou;

sentences.zh: 次月魯，江浙行省理問官。

translations.literal: Second Yuelu, investigative officer of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: the second, Yuelu, investigative officer of the Jiang-Zhe Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 伯忽，夔州路總管，天曆初，囊加台據蜀叛，死於難，特贈推忠秉義效節功臣、資善大夫、中書右丞、上護軍，追封蜀郡公，諡忠愍。

translations.literal: Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit; at the beginning of Tianli Nangjiatai held Shu in rebellion; he died in the calamity; specially posthumously given Merit Subject of Exerting Loyalty and Upholding Righteousness in Devoted Service, Grand Master of Assisting Goodness, Right Vice Administrator of the Secretariat, Upper Protector of the Army, posthumously enfeoffed Duke of Shu Commandery, posthumous name Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: and Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou—in the early Tianli era, when Nangjiatai rebelled in Sichuan, he died in the uprising and was posthumously honored as Loyal Merit Subject, Grand Master of Assisting Goodness, vice administrator of the Secretariat, and Duke of Shu with the temple name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 孔思晦

translations.literal: Kong Sihui
translations.idiomatic: Kong Sihui

sentences.zh: 孔思晦，字明道，孔子五十四世孫也。

translations.literal: Kong Sihui, style name Mingdao, was the fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Sihui, whose style was Mingdao, was the fifty-fourth-generation descendant of Confucius.

sentences.zh: 資質端重，而性簡默，童丱時，讀書已識大義。

translations.literal: His nature and bearing were upright and weighty, while his character was simple and silent; in childhood when studying books he already understood great principles.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and grave in bearing, quiet by nature, he grasped the larger meaning of texts even as a child.

sentences.zh: 及長，授業於導江張，講求義理，於詞章之習，薄而弗為。

translations.literal: When grown, he received instruction from Zhang Zhihan of Daojiang, pursued inquiry into moral principle, and toward the practice of literary composition was sparing and did not engage in it.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he studied under Zhang Zhihan of Daojiang, pursuing moral principle while disdaining mere literary ornament.

sentences.zh: 家貧，躬耕以為養，雖劇寒暑，而為學未嘗懈，遠近爭聘為子弟師。

translations.literal: His family was poor; he personally plowed to support them; though heat and cold were extreme, in study he never slackened; near and far competed to hire him as teacher of their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor and he farmed to support them, he never slackened in study through the harshest seasons, and neighbors near and far vied to hire him as a tutor.

sentences.zh: 大德中，遊京師，祭酒耶律有尚欲薦之，以母老，辭而歸。

translations.literal: In the Dade period he traveled to the capital; libationer Yelü Youshang wished to recommend him, but because his mother was old he declined and returned.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dade era he traveled to the capital, where libationer Yelü Youshang wished to recommend him; he declined and returned because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 母臥疾，躬進藥餌，衣不解帶。

translations.literal: When his mother lay ill, he personally brought medicine and food, and did not remove his belt from his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill he personally tended her medicine and food and never undressed for rest.

sentences.zh: 居喪，勺水不入口者五日。

translations.literal: In mourning he did not take a spoonful of water into his mouth for five days.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he took no food or water for five days.

sentences.zh: 至大中，舉茂才，為范陽儒學教諭。

translations.literal: In Dazhong he was nominated as Maocai and made Confucian instructor of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dazhong era he was nominated as an outstanding scholar and appointed Confucian instructor at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 延祐初，調寧陽學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yanyou he was transferred to Ningyang school.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yanyou era he was transferred to the school at Ningyang.

sentences.zh: 先是，兩縣校官率以廩薄不能守職，而思晦以儉約自將，教養有法，比代去，學者皆不忍舍之。

translations.literal: Previously the school officials of both counties mostly because stipends were thin could not hold their posts, while Sihui with frugality and restraint conducted himself, had methods in teaching and nurturing, and when successive replacements left, students all could not bear to part from him.
translations.idiomatic: School officers in both counties had typically failed to hold their posts because stipends were too meager, but Kong Sihui lived frugally and taught with method; when the time came for rotation, students were unwilling to see him go.

sentences.zh: 於是孔氏族人相與議：思晦嫡長且賢，宜襲封爵，奉祠事。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Kong clan kinsmen deliberated together: Sihui was the legitimate eldest and also worthy—he ought to inherit enfeoffment and title, and undertake sacrificial duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Kong clansmen then agreed that Sihui, as the legitimate eldest son and a man of virtue, should inherit the hereditary title and oversee the ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 狀上政府，事未決。

translations.literal: A petition was sent up to the government; the matter was not yet settled.
translations.idiomatic: They submitted a petition to the authorities, but the matter remained undecided.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在位，雅崇尚儒道，一日，問：「孔子之裔今幾世，襲爵為誰？

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong was on the throne and greatly honored the Confucian Way; one day he asked: "Confucius's descendants are now how many generations, and who holds the inherited title?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong, a devoted patron of Confucian learning, one day asked, "How many generations removed are Confucius's descendants today, and who holds the hereditary title?"

sentences.zh: 」廷臣具對曰：「未定。

translations.literal: Court ministers replied in detail saying: "Not yet settled."
translations.idiomatic: The court ministers answered together, "That has not yet been decided."

sentences.zh: 」帝親取孔氏譜牒按之，曰：「以嫡應襲封者，思晦也，复奚疑！

translations.literal: The emperor personally took the Kong clan genealogical registers and examined them, saying, "The one who by lineal right should inherit the enfeoffment is Sihui—what further doubt is there!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself took out the Kong clan genealogies and said, "The legitimate heir to the title is Sihui. What room is there for doubt!"

sentences.zh: 」特授中議大夫，襲封衍聖公，月俸百緡，加至五百緡，賜四品印。

translations.literal: He was specially appointed Grand Master of Palace Discussion, inherited the enfeoffment as Duke Who Extends Sageliness, with a monthly salary of a hundred strings of cash increased to five hundred, and was given a seal of the fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was specially appointed Grand Master of Palace Discussion and invested as Duke Who Extends Sageliness, with a monthly stipend raised from one hundred to five hundred strings of cash and a fourth-rank seal.

sentences.zh: 泰定三年，山東廉訪副使王鵬南言：「襲爵上公，而階止四品，於格弗稱，且失尊崇意。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiding the Shandong Surveillance Vice Commissioner Wang Pengnan said, "He inherits a title of exalted duke, yet his rank stops at the fourth grade—this does not match the regulations and moreover fails to show due reverence."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Taiding era Wang Pengnan, vice commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, said, "He holds a ducal title of the highest honor, yet his official rank is only fourth grade. This does not match protocol and fails to show the respect due to Confucius's heir."

sentences.zh: 」明年，升嘉議大夫。

translations.literal: The next year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Grand Master of Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 至順二年，改賜三品印。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhishun he was given a seal of the third rank in place of the former one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhishun era he was granted a third-rank seal.

sentences.zh: 思晦以宗祀責重，恆懼弗勝，每遇祭祀，必敬必慎。

translations.literal: Sihui, because the responsibility for ancestral sacrifice was weighty, constantly feared he might not measure up; whenever sacrifice came due he was invariably reverent and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Sihui felt the weight of his duty to maintain the ancestral rites and constantly feared he might fall short. At every sacrifice he was scrupulously reverent.

sentences.zh: 初，廟毀於兵，後雖苟完，而角樓圍牆未備，思晦竭力營度，以復其舊。

translations.literal: At first the temple had been destroyed in war; though later patched up, the corner towers and enclosing walls were not complete—Sihui labored with all his strength to plan and restore it to its former state.
translations.idiomatic: The temple had been destroyed in war and only roughly repaired; the corner towers and walls were still incomplete. Sihui threw himself into restoring it to its former condition.

sentences.zh: 金絲堂壞，又一新之，祭器禮服，悉加整飭。

translations.literal: The Hall of Gold Threads had fallen into ruin; he rebuilt it anew, and ritual vessels and ceremonial robes were all put in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Gold Threads had collapsed; he rebuilt it and put all the ritual vessels and ceremonial robes in proper order.

sentences.zh: 又以尼山乃毓聖之地，故有廟，已毀，民冒耕祭田且百年，思晦復其田，且請置尼山書院，以列於學官，朝廷從之。

translations.literal: Moreover, since Mount Ni was the place where the Sage was nurtured, there had been a temple there which was already destroyed; commoners had encroached on and farmed the sacrificial fields for nearly a hundred years—Sihui recovered the fields and also requested establishment of a Mount Ni Academy to be listed among the official schools; the court approved.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Ni, where the Sage had been born, also had a ruined temple, and for nearly a century local people had illegally farmed the sacrificial lands. Sihui recovered the fields and petitioned to establish a Mount Ni Academy under the official school system. The court approved.

sentences.zh: 三氏學舊有田三千畝，佔於豪民，子思書院舊有營運錢萬緡，貸於民取子錢，以供祭祀，久之，民不輸子錢，並負其本，思晦皆理而復之。

translations.literal: The Three Clans School formerly had three thousand mu of fields seized by powerful families; the Zisi Academy formerly had ten thousand strings of operating funds lent to the people at interest to supply sacrifices—for a long time the people paid no interest and also owed the principal—Sihui settled all these matters and restored them.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand mu of land belonging to the Three Clans School had been seized by powerful families, and ten thousand strings of operating funds from the Zisi Academy had been lent out at interest for sacrificial expenses. Borrowers had long ceased paying interest and even defaulted on the principal. Sihui recovered everything through legal settlement.

sentences.zh: 聖父舊封齊國公，思晦言於朝曰：「宣聖封王，而父爵猶公，願加褒崇。

translations.literal: The Sage's father had formerly been enfeoffed as Duke of Qi; Sihui said at court, "The Sagely Exemplar is enfeoffed as king, yet his father's title is still duke—I wish to add further honor."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius's father had long held the title Duke of Qi. Sihui said at court, "The Sagely Exemplar has been enfeoffed as a king, yet his father remains only a duke. I ask that greater honor be granted."

sentences.zh: 」乃詔加封聖父啟聖王，聖母王夫人。

translations.literal: An edict thereupon added the enfeoffment of the Sage's father as King Who Initiated Sageliness and the Sage's mother as Lady Wang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict thereupon ennobled the Sage's father as King Who Initiated Sageliness and his mother as Lady Wang.

sentences.zh: 五季時，孔末之後方盛，欲以偽滅真，害宣聖子孫幾盡，至是，其裔复欲冒稱宣聖後。

translations.literal: In the Five Dynasties period the descendants of Kong Mo had been flourishing, wishing to destroy the true line with the false and nearly exterminating the Sagely Exemplar's descendants; at this time their offspring again wished to pass themselves off as descendants of the Sagely Exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties the descendants of Kong Mo had nearly wiped out the true line of Confucius in their bid to supplant it. Now their descendants again tried to pass themselves off as Confucius's heirs.

sentences.zh: 思晦以為：「不早辨則真偽久益不可明，彼與我不共戴天，乃列於族，與共拜殿庭，可乎？

translations.literal: Sihui considered: "If we do not distinguish early, true and false will long grow ever harder to clarify—they and I are irreconcilable enemies; can they be listed in the clan and worship together in the hall?"
translations.idiomatic: Sihui said, "If we do not settle this now, the true line and the impostors will only grow harder to tell apart. They are our hereditary enemies. How can they be enrolled in the clan and worship with us in the temple hall?"

sentences.zh: 」遂會族人，稽典故斥之，既又重刻宗譜於石，而孔氏族裔益明矣。

translations.literal: He thereupon assembled the clansmen, investigated classical precedents and rejected them, and afterward had the clan genealogy carved anew in stone, so that the Kong clan descent became still clearer.
translations.idiomatic: He convened the clan, cited precedent to reject them, and had the genealogy recarved in stone, making the true Kong lineage unmistakably clear.

sentences.zh: 元統元年卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong he died, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of the Yuantong era at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，有鶴百餘翔其屋上，又見神光自東南落其舍北。

translations.literal: On the day of his death more than a hundred cranes circled above his house, and a divine light was seen falling from the southeast upon the north side of his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died more than a hundred cranes circled above his house, and a supernatural light was seen descending from the southeast onto the north side of his home.

sentences.zh: 至正中，朝廷加贈其官，而賜諡曰文肅。

translations.literal: In the Zhizheng period the court added posthumous offices and granted the posthumous name Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhizheng era the court added posthumous honors and gave him the posthumous name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 子曰克堅，襲封衍聖公，階嘉議大夫，既而進通奉大夫。

translations.literal: His son was named Kejian; he inherited the enfeoffment as Duke Who Extends Sageliness, with the rank of Grand Master of Court Discussion, and was later promoted to Grand Master for Imperial Service.
translations.idiomatic: His son Kejian inherited the title Duke Who Extends Sageliness at the rank of Grand Master of Court Discussion and was later promoted to Grand Master for Imperial Service.

sentences.zh: 至正十五年，召為同知太常禮儀院事，拜陝西行臺侍御史，遷國子祭酒，擢山東肅政廉訪使，不赴。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Zhizheng he was summoned as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, appointed Attending Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial University, and promoted to Commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, but he did not take up the last post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of the Zhizheng era he was summoned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, made attending censor of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, then chancellor of the Imperial University, and finally promoted to commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 孫希學，襲封衍聖公。

translations.literal: His grandson Xixue inherited the enfeoffment as Duke Who Extends Sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Xixue inherited the title Duke Who Extends Sageliness.
